answer: The Great Fire of London started in the early hours of 2 September 1666 at Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane. The exact cause is unknown, but it most likely came from his oven, either a spark landing on fuel stored nearby or an oven that hadn't been fully put out, though Farriner said he had raked it out properly [1][2][3]. The fire spread quickly because the summer had been hot and dry with weeks of no rain. Most houses were built of timber and packed along narrow streets, and the warehouses on nearby Thames Street held timber, rope and oil. A strong east wind then blew the flames from house to house and turned the blaze into an inferno [2][3][4]. It burned for about four days, destroyed roughly 13,200 houses and left about 100,000 people homeless. A Frenchman named Robert Hubert was wrongly hanged for starting it [3][4].
